label: late original-phase positions (t>=5) and the <DEL> step, gated by sequence content
explanation: Fires only in the original phase and on the <DEL> step: never at t<=2, rarely at t=3-4, and most often at t=5-8 (88% of mass in the original phase, 12% on <DEL>). It essentially never fires in the copy phase (11 steps out of 546k). The firing rate climbs with absolute position (orig_idx 8 is 46% vs 1% at orig_idx 3), so longer sequences (L=8-9) carry 75% of the mass. Within that window it fires on only about a quarter of steps. Which steps it picks depends on sequence content in a distributed way: it is stronger when the first token is d/h/y/w/v, on inputs p/o/f/j, and on first occurrences of a token (in_first). No simple token-set predicate captured that content dependence; adding first-token or seen-token conditions raised precision to about 0.5 but cut recall roughly in half. Top activations are runs of rising activation in the last few original steps (often peaking on p/o) followed by a strong <DEL> step. The predicate has high recall and mass recall (about 0.9) but low precision (about 0.23).
